summary: A receipt-bound 0.2.89 development extension ran in an admitted isolated Chrome-for-Testing guest profile. The native side panel showed the five guest navigation tabs and 11 recognized Settings section labels. These are visibility observations only.

verification.evidence: Chat, Scrape, Data, SEO and Settings were the five visible navigation buttons, matching source audience 'everyone'. Other roles/tabs were not exercised.

11 expected guest section labels and 14 known labels were visible. The query found 16 visible button[aria-expanded] elements total; five were unclassified by the fixed label list and are not established as section headers. Per-section descendant counts are in the run receipt and are not authoritative control counts.

role_matrix.guest: Navigation and visible Settings labels observed in a fresh isolated profile.

build_and_guard.resource_guard: admitted on external scratch; child exit 0; lease released

limitations: The primary Chrome installation and Store extension state remain unverified because primary-profile free disk was below the guard minimum.
The five unclassified expanded-state buttons were counted without returning their labels; no claim is made that they are section headings.
Visibility does not prove control behavior, persistence, permission behavior, or backend effects. No behavioral pass was recorded.
A fresh profile provided no member/admin state; no user profile was copied and no credentials were entered.
next_action: Root reconciles these observations with EXT-F-1001 and EXT-F-1003. The source/visible inventory gate remains open for unclassified controls and member/admin coverage; only root may open behavioral testing.
